title: Preserved book failure boundary and bounded replacement controls
question: What do the original receipts establish about settlement durability, nested uncertainty and discovery, and what still requires live bounded confirmation?
method: Read the three held managed manifests and their existing durable artifacts, export the original sealed book journal, verify its digest and summarize it without opening a database. Compare named replacement native controls within their recorded scope. Managed native enrichment reported unavailable, so infer no current intent standing.
commands: uv run ci results inspect 1dd5d45ded4b4ea38399fb121a44d28c --view observations --severity ERROR --limit 100 --max-bytes 1048576 --examined-bytes 1048576 --json
uv run ci results export 1dd5d45ded4b4ea38399fb121a44d28c --role observations --destination docs/design_review/evidence/2026-11-19_udm20-retained-diagnosis/raw/book-observations.jsonl --json

results.name: aggregate_reported_subexceptions
results.note: Nested group detail is explicitly omitted; this does not identify the additional nested uncertainty.

results.name: settlement_statement_timeout_events
results.note: SQLSTATE 57014 and server statement-timeout message, not measured per-statement duration.

results.name: last_pinned_committed_intent_inspections
results.note: Historical last-pinned observations, not a fresh final-state census or proof that an unresolved intent is absent.

conclusion: Original failure outcomes and the exact sealed journal are preserved. The nine statement cancellations locate failure during retain-intent digest/seal work before that statement added a committed intake; separate runtime and release failures are also present. Bounded native controls establish durable answer/intent reconciliation and compatible discovery/selection, but do not reproduce unknown network commit, recover the original unresolved intent, establish all nine region sizes, isolate book SQL cost, or qualify final stage/book behavior. Original canonical and bounded stage targets are explicitly distinct.
